output.brief: The Android drop is not caused by release 6.14. A Corvane rule-pack update on 3 March at 10:38 UTC added a rule, AUTO-LIB-17. It blocks any request from the app's networking library (nettle-http) to the password-login path when there is no edge session cookie. Blocking began at 10:41, on every app version at once, and about 9,600 requests a day are blocked. Those requests carry Android app-install IDs, and 92% of the installs had a successful login in the prior 90 days, so they are real customers. Quick-unlock, iOS and web are untouched. Password success fell from 96% to 8%. The OS patch, the auth token change and credential stuffing don't fit the evidence. The 6.14 rollout is only 5–10% of users and shows the same failure rate as older versions. I'm highly confident. Next step: have Corvane set only the new rule to log-only on the mobile password path. Keep rate limits, lockout and the other rules on. Then confirm in telemetry that password success recovers. Don't roll back 6.14, don't raise bot sensitivity, and don't exclude blocked attempts from the KPI. Ask Corvane to explain the rule and the lack of testing for vendor updates. The contact-centre call increase is only loosely tied to the drop, since fee notices also went out that week.
